newsitem.title: UK: LME post-Sumitomo reforms "excellent" - Asarco CEO.
newsitem.headline: LME post-Sumitomo reforms "excellent" - Asarco CEO.

text.p: Changes instituted by the London Metal Exchange (LME), following the Sumitomo Corp scandal were described as "excellent" by ASARCO Inc President and Chief Executive Officer Richard de J. Osbourne.
"I think they are excellent. Daily reporting of stocks eliminates uncertainty and puts more facts into the market," Osbourne told reporters after a briefing.
The LME is currently instituting widespread reforms recommended by Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) late last year. These include wider transparancy.
Osbourne said that the copper market would have been better served by clearer information at the time of the Sumitomo scandal.
"Real damage was done to the market, and Sumitomo should have stepped forward with more information," he said.
However, Sumitomo did not know themselves what was going on in copper, which at times in 1996, not only lacked information, but was also subject to wild statements on so-called "hidden stocks".
"Large positions ought to be common knowledge in the market...It would have benefited from much more disclosure," Osbourne added.
